summary: The refactor drops the 500-character length limit on notes, so unbounded text can be stored, and it deletes the test that caught it. Files read: src/store.mjs and test/notes.test.mjs in full, main:src/store.mjs as the base, and the callers src/server.mjs (POST /notes -> store.create), src/client.mjs (add) and test/helpers.mjs. grep for MAX_TEXT and validateText finds no other users.

findings.issue: This is labeled a refactor but it changes behavior. The base create() also rejected text longer than MAX_TEXT with a 400 ('text is longer than 500 characters'). That check was not carried into validateText(), so POST /notes now accepts text of any length. Every note stays in the in-memory Map for the life of the process, so any valid token holder can grow memory without limit (a denial-of-service path). It also breaks the API contract: outside callers that relied on the 400 for text over 500 characters now get a 201.
findings.fix: Move the length check into validateText(): `if (text.length > MAX_TEXT) throw new StoreError(400, `text is longer than ${MAX_TEXT} characters`)` right after the empty/type check, so the refactor keeps the same behavior.

findings.issue: The test was weakened so the regression would pass. The assertion that a 501-character note returns 400 was removed and the test renamed to leave out 'too-long'. This breaks the house rule 'never weaken a test to make it pass'. Nothing now covers the length limit.
findings.fix: Put back `assert.equal((await raw(app.base, 'POST', '/notes', { body: JSON.stringify({ text: 'x'.repeat(501) }) })).status, 400)` and the name 'empty and too-long notes are rejected'. Keeping the new whitespace-only assertion is fine. Adding a check that exactly 500 characters returns 201 would pin the boundary.

findings.issue: MAX_TEXT is now dead code: nothing reads it after the length check was dropped. It makes the file look like a limit is still enforced when none is.
findings.fix: Resolved by the first fix, which makes validateText() read MAX_TEXT again. Do not delete the constant.

pre_existing.code:
const body = await readJson(req)
        return send(res, 201, store.create(user, body.text))
pre_existing.issue: A JSON body of `null` makes JSON.parse return null, so body.text throws a TypeError. The catch returns a generic 500 instead of a 4xx JSON error, which breaks the house rule that a bad request gets a 4xx.
readJson() buffers the whole request body with no size cap, even before any text-length check runs. An authenticated caller can send a very large body to use up memory.
